<h1 class="widget__headline h1">
<a aria-label="Trump Stunk Up This Criminal Justice Forum, So Kamala Harris Went And Got Her Own" class="widget__headline-text custom-post-headline" href="https://www.wonkette.com/trump-stunk-up-this-criminal-justice-forum-so-kamala-harris-went-and-got-her-own">
    Trump Stunk Up This Criminal Justice Forum, So Kamala Harris Went And Got Her Own
</a></h1>
<div class="widget__subheadline">
<h2 class="widget__subheadline-text h2"><p>Trump, naturally, is throwing a conniption fit. </p></h2>
</div>
<div class="social-author clearfix">
<div class="social-author__avatar image">
<div class="cover-all image" style='background-image: url("https://assets.rbl.ms/17399306/210x.jpg")'></div>
</div>
<a class="social-author__name" href="https://www.wonkette.com/u/robyn_pennacchia">Robyn Pennacchia</a>
</div>
<div class="social-date">
<span class="social-date__text">October 26, 2019 12:33 PM</span>
</div>
<div class="body js-expandable clearfix js-listicle-body css-listicle-body-2641113503">
<div class="body-description"><div class="widget__brief"><p>On Friday night, Kamala Harris announced that she would be pulling out of a criminal justice reform forum at Benedict College in Columbia, South Carolina, an HBCU, in protest of the fact that the organizers of said forum, the 20/20 Bipartisan Justice Center, gave Donald Trump a "Bipartisan Justice Award" on Friday in a ceremony that only seven students were even allowed to attend. </p><p>Harris' team sent out the following email on Friday night:</p><blockquote style="margin-left: 20px;">As Trump Is Awarded Despite Decades of Shameful Actions on Justice Issues and Students Are Excluded From Participating, Kamala Harris Pulls Out Of 2019 Second Step Presidential Justice Forum<br/>Harris will instead discuss criminal justice reform at open event with students and the broader community in Columbia<br/><br/>Tomorrow, October 26, Senator Kamala Harris will join students and the broader Columbia community to discuss criminal justice reform instead of participating in the 2019 Second Step Presidential Justice Forum at Benedict College.<br/><br/>"As the only candidate who attended an HBCU, I know the importance that these spaces hold for young Black Americans," said Harris. "Today, when it became clear Donald Trump would receive an award after decades of celebrating mass incarceration, pushing the death penalty for innocent Black Americans, rolling back police accountability measures and racist behavior that puts people's lives at risk, and then learned all but ten Benedict students are excluded from participating, I cannot in good faith be complicit in papering over his record. Instead, I'll host students from all campuses as well as the broader Columbia community to come and discuss this critical issue that I've worked on for my entire career.<br/><br/>"Donald Trump is a lawless President. Not only does he circumvent the laws of our country and the principles of our Constitution, but there is nothing in his career that is about justice, for justice, or in celebration of justice."</blockquote></div>
<div class="js-appear-on-expand">
<script type="keep-reading-content">&lt;p&gt;While one&#39;s first instinct might be to go &#34;Oh no, what are you doing? Yes, it&#39;s gross that they gave Trump an award but it also seems like a bad idea, tactically, to skip any forums at this point!,&#34; the whole thing has very much worked in her favor. Not only is she holding a roundtable discussion on criminal justice reform with students and residents of Columbia on her own today at 2pm, the mayor of Columbia is also setting up &lt;em&gt;another&lt;/em&gt;, separate criminal justice reform forum at Benedict College that will not be tainted by the likes of Donald Trump. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Via &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.apnews.com/e0b6a1005252446cbc6b84872ec6e418&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;AP&lt;/a&gt;:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;Soon after her announcement, the mayor of South Carolina&#39;s capital city, Columbia, and a co-host of the event said he was organizing an alternative forum at Benedict College, a historically black college, for any candidates who wished to participate, with Harris&#39; campaign confirming she would be among them.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&#34;I honestly wanted to give everyone else another option,&#34; Columbia Mayor Steve Benjamin told The Associated Press about his event, which will be held with the theme &#34;Students First&#34; in a college chapel.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;As of Friday night, Benjamin said Cory Booker and Joe Biden, and likely Bernie Sanders, planned to attend his event, as well as the original forum.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;So, as it turns out, this was quite the baller move. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;As Donald Trump is always looking for new and exciting ways to be terrible, he weighed in on the whole thing this morning with a few extremely stupid tweets. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class=&#34;shortcode-media shortcode-media-twitter_embed&#34;&gt;
        &lt;iframe width=&#34;100%&#34; height=&#34;150&#34; scrolling=&#34;no&#34; id=&#34;twitter-embed-1188067369501052929&#34; src=&#34;/res/community/twitter_embed/?iframe_id=twitter-embed-1188067369501052929&amp;created_ts=1572092308.0&amp;screen_name=realDonaldTrump&amp;text=....greatly+help+the+African+American+community+%28and+all+other+communities%29%2C+and+which+was+unable+to+get+done+in+pa%E2%80%A6+https%3A%2F%2Ft.co%2FYyLJdoDkk3&amp;id=1188067369501052929&amp;name=Donald+J.+Trump&#34; frameborder=&#34;0&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;ESA03D1572110691&#34;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;
        &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;It should be noted, again, that nearly all the seats at Trump&#39;s award ceremony were reserved for the administration and their guests, and that there were spots for only 10 students, only seven of whom actually showed up. All of the other students were required to stay in their dorms. Given this, one could assume that the vast majority of actual black people who showed up to the ceremony were &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/elections/2019/10/25/trump-speaks-hbcu-benedict-college-students-asked-stay-dorms/2462497001/&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;those who were outside of it, protesting&lt;/a&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;UPDATE: The organization that gave the award to Trump has been removed as a sponsor of the forum. Yet more proof that &#34;you don&#39;t ask, you don&#39;t get.&lt;/p&gt;
        &lt;p class=&#34;shortcode-media shortcode-media-twitter_embed&#34;&gt;
        &lt;iframe width=&#34;100%&#34; height=&#34;150&#34; scrolling=&#34;no&#34; id=&#34;twitter-embed-1188128169230032897&#34; src=&#34;/res/community/twitter_embed/?iframe_id=twitter-embed-1188128169230032897&amp;created_ts=1572106804.0&amp;screen_name=IanSams&amp;text=UPDATE+%26gt%3B%26gt%3B+Because+of+Kamala%E2%80%99s+protest%2C+the+sponsor+that+awarded+Trump+has+been+completely+removed+from+this+event+a%E2%80%A6+https%3A%2F%2Ft.co%2F1G2V6pp7WV&amp;id=1188128169230032897&amp;name=Ian+Sams&#34; frameborder=&#34;0&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;3H15WR1572110691&#34;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;
        &lt;/p&gt;
        &lt;p&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;[&lt;a href=&#34;https://www.apnews.com/e0b6a1005252446cbc6b84872ec6e418&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;AP&lt;/a&gt;]&lt;/p&gt;
                </script>
</div>

<h1 class="widget__headline h1">
<a aria-label="Tulsi Gabbard Puts On Her Robe And Her Wizard Hat" class="widget__headline-text custom-post-headline" href="https://www.wonkette.com/tulsi-gabbard-puts-on-her-robe-and-her-wizard-hat">
    Tulsi Gabbard Puts On Her Robe And Her Wizard Hat
</a></h1>
<div class="widget__subheadline">
<h2 class="widget__subheadline-text h2"><p>She's quitting Congress, gonna spend the next year LARP-fighting her life-sized cut-out of Hillary Clinton, we guess.</p></h2>
</div>
<div class="social-author clearfix">
<div class="social-author__avatar image">
<div class="cover-all image" style='background-image: url("https://assets.rbl.ms/18110596/210x.jpg")'></div>
</div>
<a class="social-author__name" href="https://www.wonkette.com/u/evan_hurst">Evan Hurst</a>
</div>
<div class="social-date">
<span class="social-date__text">October 25, 2019 04:15 PM</span>
</div>
<div class="body js-expandable clearfix js-listicle-body css-listicle-body-2641105245">
<div class="body-description"><div class="widget__brief"><p>Send many weepy alohas to Hawaii's second Congressional District, because Tulsi Gabbard has announced she will not be running for Congress again in 2020. (Super-cool dude named Kai Kahele was probably gonna beat her in the primary anyway. <a href="https://www.kaikahele.com/" target="_blank">Donate him here!</a>) Instead, she is very focused on losing the Democratic primary, where she is polling at approximately LOL percent, and dueling with Hillary Clinton in the imaginary presidential election that's happening in her mind. After that, maybe she will do a third-party spoiler run, so that we can all be assured that Hillary Clinton was <em>exactly</em> right <a href="https://www.wonkette.com/hillary-clinton-said-true-thing-about-tulsi-gabbard-everybody-sh-t-your-pants" target="_blank">when she called Gabbard</a> a Republican asset without actually saying Gabbard's name. (She SWEARS she's not gonna do that. She SWEARS.)  <br/></p></div>
<div class="js-appear-on-expand">
<script type="keep-reading-content">&lt;p&gt;Gabbard posted a bunch of garbage on Twitter last night in announcing her intention to stop Congressing:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class=&#34;shortcode-media shortcode-media-twitter_embed&#34;&gt;
        &lt;iframe width=&#34;100%&#34; height=&#34;150&#34; scrolling=&#34;no&#34; id=&#34;twitter-embed-1187579717630623745&#34; src=&#34;/res/community/twitter_embed/?iframe_id=twitter-embed-1187579717630623745&amp;created_ts=1571976043.0&amp;screen_name=TulsiGabbard&amp;text=I%27m+so+grateful+to+the+people+of+Hawai%CA%BBi+for+allowing+me+to+serve+you+in+Congress+for+the+last+7+years.+Throughout%E2%80%A6+https%3A%2F%2Ft.co%2FQtqUrkpcaA&amp;id=1187579717630623745&amp;name=Tulsi+Gabbard&#34; frameborder=&#34;0&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;T4I6VW1572037525&#34;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;
        &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;She &lt;a href=&#34;https://twitter.com/TulsiGabbard/status/1187706669683183616&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;posted more garbage&lt;/a&gt; this morning announcing her intention to quit Congress, acting as if this was first announcement of it, even though she also posted it last night. It is all very interesting garbage, we are sure.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;On Tuesday, Gabbard posted a very angry video about how Hillary Clinton ruined the world, demanding Hillary descend from her &#34;throne&#34; so Gabbard can catch her with this Poké Ball and Razz Berry right here.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class=&#34;shortcode-media shortcode-media-twitter_embed&#34;&gt;
        &lt;iframe width=&#34;100%&#34; height=&#34;150&#34; scrolling=&#34;no&#34; id=&#34;twitter-embed-1186763222193299457&#34; src=&#34;/res/community/twitter_embed/?iframe_id=twitter-embed-1186763222193299457&amp;created_ts=1571781375.0&amp;screen_name=TulsiGabbard&amp;text=.%40HillaryClinton%2C+your+foreign+policy+was+a+disaster+for+our+country+and+the+world.+It%E2%80%99s+time+for+you+to+acknowledg%E2%80%A6+https%3A%2F%2Ft.co%2Fr5QxZnZw5P&amp;id=1186763222193299457&amp;name=Tulsi+Gabbard&#34; frameborder=&#34;0&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;JRM6JU1572037525&#34;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;
        &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;On Wednesday, Gabbard posted the very same angry video about how Hillary Clinton ruined the world, demanding Hillary descend from her throne, GOTTA CATCH &#39;EM ALL, TULSI!&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class=&#34;shortcode-media shortcode-media-twitter_embed&#34;&gt;
        &lt;iframe width=&#34;100%&#34; height=&#34;150&#34; scrolling=&#34;no&#34; id=&#34;twitter-embed-1186937436531675137&#34; src=&#34;/res/community/twitter_embed/?iframe_id=twitter-embed-1186937436531675137&amp;created_ts=1571822911.0&amp;screen_name=TulsiGabbard&amp;text=.%40HillaryClinton%2C+your+foreign+policy+was+a+disaster+for+our+country+and+the+world.+It%E2%80%99s+time+for+you+to+acknowledg%E2%80%A6+https%3A%2F%2Ft.co%2FDSwYSbShvk&amp;id=1186937436531675137&amp;name=Tulsi+Gabbard&#34; frameborder=&#34;0&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;LCXXTE1572037525&#34;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;
        &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Trouble for Tulsi Gabbard, of course, is that despite the fact that her race against Hillary Clinton is happening entirely in Imagination Land, and despite how verily she has &lt;a href=&#34;https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/i-put-on-my-robe-and-wizard-hat&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;put on her robe and her wizard hat,&lt;/a&gt; she is actually losing that primary too, according to exclusive Wonkette reporting on recent polls taken by denizens of Tulsi Gabbard&#39;s daydreams.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;On Thursday night, Gabbard was &lt;a href=&#34;https://iowastartingline.com/2019/10/25/gabbard-skips-iowa-forum-appears-on-fox-news-instead/&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;supposed to be doing&lt;/a&gt; a Latino town hall in Iowa, like a person running for the Democratic nomination for president of the United States. Instead she went on Hannity, like a Russian asset being groomed by Republicans to run as a third-party spoiler. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;And guess what she was upset about NO GUESS, THREE GUESSES!&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;If you guessed, &#34;She is mad at Democrats for lack of transparency in the impeachment process, using the same bullshit debunked talking points as Matt Gaetz did &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.wonkette.com/matt-gaetzs-moron-rebellion-leaves-mark-on-impeachment-inquiry-a-skidmark&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;when he was doing skidmarks&lt;/a&gt; to the impeachment inquiry with the House Freedom Caucus Republicans,&#34; award yourself a sexxxy prize!&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class=&#34;shortcode-media shortcode-media-twitter_embed&#34;&gt;
        &lt;iframe width=&#34;100%&#34; height=&#34;150&#34; scrolling=&#34;no&#34; id=&#34;twitter-embed-1187544241427214336&#34; src=&#34;/res/community/twitter_embed/?iframe_id=twitter-embed-1187544241427214336&amp;created_ts=1571967585.0&amp;screen_name=Acyn&amp;text=Tulsi+Gabbard+appears+on+Hannity+and+criticizes+the+impeachment+inquiry+process+by+saying+she+doesn%E2%80%99t+know+what%E2%80%99s+g%E2%80%A6+https%3A%2F%2Ft.co%2FfsJxYfqNfI&amp;id=1187544241427214336&amp;name=Acyn+Torabi&#34; frameborder=&#34;0&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;0SKKIN1572037525&#34;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;
        &lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;&#34;I don&#39;t know what&#39;s going on in those closed-doors. We, as members of Congress, don&#39;t have access to the information that is being shared. And I think the American people deserve to know exactly what the facts are.&#34;&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;Sounds like Aunt Wizard Hat needs to read &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.wonkette.com/trump-officials-in-mad-dash-to-spill-it-to-impeachment-investigators&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Wonkette&#39;s letter to Uncle Walter&lt;/a&gt; about the six things idiots don&#39;t understand about impeachment. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;If you&#39;d like to watch the entire Hannity appearance, &lt;a href=&#34;https://video.foxnews.com/v/6097532867001/#sp=show-clips&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;you may clicketh here.&lt;/a&gt; Gabbard got in some good zingers about how President Hillary Clinton is sending bad messages to our soldiers, we guess because Hillary isn&#39;t &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.wonkette.com/tulsi-gabbard-brings-friend-to-debate-oh-f-ck-its-assad&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;BFFs with Assad&lt;/a&gt; or something, we dunno, didn&#39;t feel like watching the whole thing.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;We will give Tulsi Gabbard credit for one thing. When Sean Hannity went on his acid trip about Hunter Biden and Ukraine and China, she did not bite. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;She and Hannity really got along, though. Just like she and Tucker Carlson &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.wonkette.com/if-its-what-you-say-tulsi-gabbard-loves-it-especially-later-in-the-summer&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;really get along.&lt;/a&gt; Golly what a Democrat she is. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;She concluded by saying she and Sean Hannity probably &lt;em&gt;don&#39;t&lt;/em&gt; have a lot in common, EXCEPT:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;You and I agree on one very important point, and that is that the American people have had enough of Hillary Clinton and her warmongering policies.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;Then she tried to do a moneybeg and Sean Hannity cut her off and it was pretty funny.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Hillary Clinton responded by going to Elijah Cummings&#39;s funeral and then going out for lunch or something, on account of how, though she may be living rent-free in Tulsi Gabbard&#39;s head, she is actually not running for president. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;In summary and in conclusion, we hate the new Jill Stein. <h1 class="widget__headline h1">
<a aria-label="Trump Gutted Cyber Defenses, Now The FBI Needs YOU!" class="widget__headline-text custom-post-headline" href="https://www.wonkette.com/2020-white-house-hacking-videos">
    Trump Gutted Cyber Defenses, Now The FBI Needs YOU!
</a></h1>
<div class="widget__subheadline">
<h2 class="widget__subheadline-text h2"><p>Only You Can Prevent Russian Fuckery In 2020. <br/></p></h2>
</div>
<div class="social-author clearfix">
<div class="social-author__avatar image">
<div class="cover-all image" style='background-image: url("https://assets.rbl.ms/18038171/210x.jpg")'></div>
</div>
<a class="social-author__name" href="https://www.wonkette.com/u/dominic_gwinn">Dominic Gwinn</a>
</div>
<div class="social-date">
<span class="social-date__text">October 25, 2019 03:40 PM</span>
</div>
<div class="body js-expandable clearfix js-listicle-body css-listicle-body-2641104915">
<div class="body-description"><div class="widget__brief"><p>As the Trump administration tells Americans not to worry about the creepy Russians knocking on our back door, the FBI has launched a video series to help 2020 candidates up and down ballot. The videos' messages seem to confirm everything the Trump White House and congressional Republicans say isn't happening -- that Eurotrash dudes are still trying to screw with US elections. Strangely, the FBI's videos come just as the administration forces out the very super nerds whose sole mission is to protect the White House from cyber threats. </p><p>Huh!</p></div>
<div class="js-appear-on-expand">
<script type="keep-reading-content">&lt;p rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34;&gt;
	The other day Axios gossiped that the Trump administration had been busy gutting a rather important branch of &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.axios.com/scoop-cyber-memo-warns-of-new-risks-to-white-house-network-9aa19c6c-77a3-485b-919b-1dd9bd691514.html&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;the White House cyber defense team.&lt;/a&gt; Back in July, the Office of the Chief Information Security Officer (OCISO) was crammed into the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) because ... reasons. In a scathing memo/resignation letter from Dimitrios Vastakis dated Oct. 17, the now-former Branch Chief of White House Computer Network Defense writes in so many words that the White House is setting itself up to get hacked. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34;&gt;Vastakis complains that the people who work at OCISO are &#34;systematically being targeted for removal,&#34; and that the administration has been removing their duties, access to programs, buildings, and authority to make strategic decisions, as well as being a pack of wild assholes. Vastakis says the administration&#39;s plan to move the OCISO out of the Executive Office of the President -- against the recommendation of the Office of Administration Office of General Counsel (OA OGC) -- was fucked.  Vastakis adds that the administration&#39;s plan to lump &#34;the entire [White House] cybersecurity apparatus&#34; in with a group of assholes who didn&#39;t have access to presidential records was doubly fucked, and it was &#34;allowing for a large portion of institutional knowledge to concurrently walk right out the front door contrary to the best interests of the mission and the organization as a whole.&#34;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34;&gt;The OCISO was created after &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/national-security/hackers-breach-some-white-house-computers/2014/10/28/2ddf2fa0-5ef7-11e4-91f7-5d89b5e8c251_story.html&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Russia managed to hack&lt;/a&gt; into an unclassified White House network in 2014. Their specific mission was to make sure that NEVER happened again. And while it may just be a coincidence, the OCSIO does fall under the control of self-described &#34;right wing nut&#34; Mick Mulvaney -- a man who &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/16/magazine/consumer-financial-protection-bureau-trump.html&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;prides himself&lt;/a&gt; on forcing federal workers to quit , so much that he recently joked about finding &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8kbbP6I-qlA&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;&#34;a wonderful way to streamline government.&#34;&lt;/a&gt;

&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class=&#34;shortcode-media shortcode-media-youtube&#34;&gt;
        &lt;span style=&#34;display:block;position:relative;padding-top:56.25%;&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;8SFL451572123925&#34;&gt;&lt;iframe lazy-loadable=&#34;true&#34; src=&#34;https://www.youtube.com/embed/8kbbP6I-qlA?rel=0&#34; width=&#34;100%&#34; height=&#34;auto&#34; frameborder=&#34;0&#34; scrolling=&#34;no&#34; style=&#34;position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;height:100%;&#34;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;&lt;/span&gt;
        &lt;small class=&#34;image-media media-caption&#34; placeholder=&#34;Add Photo Caption...&#34;&gt;Mulvaney on Firing Federal Employees&lt;/small&gt;
        &lt;small class=&#34;image-media media-photo-credit&#34; placeholder=&#34;Add Photo Credit...&#34;&gt;
            &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8kbbP6I-qlA&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;www.youtube.com&lt;/a&gt;
        &lt;/small&gt;
        &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;This raises a whole host of questions, like WHY (in July, right around the same time Trump tried to blackmail Ukraine) would the administration want to suddenly limit access to presidential records? WHY start getting rid of the nerds whose sole job is to keep out nosy Russians? HHMMMMMMMMMMM?&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;While the Trump administration sure seems to to be trying to hide some kind of fuckery, FBI Director Chris Wray has been busy trying to make sure what happened in the 2016 election never happens again.   And to do that, he&#39;s created a bunch of videos to help people and political campaigns spot hackers. &lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;Warnings about foreign governments trying to screw with the US are nothing new. In &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.nytimes.com/2018/08/02/us/politics/russia-election-security-midterm.html&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;August of 2018&lt;/a&gt; Wray and the now quit-fired heads of the NSC, NSA, DNI, and DHS held a press gaggle to unanimously say Russia was definitely screwing with us, &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2018/07/16/us/elections/russian-interference-statements-comments.html&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;&#34;24-7 365-days-a-year.&#34;&lt;/a&gt; Twice this year Wray has gone before Congress and testified that crazy Ivans and Winnie the Poohs were trying to take all our internet bases, and that the &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.rollcall.com/news/fbi-director-wants-game-election-interference&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;US needed &#34;up our game&lt;/a&gt; to stay ahead of it.&#34; In fact, the day before Mueller &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.nytimes.com/2019/07/24/us/politics/mueller-testimony.html&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;told Congress&lt;/a&gt; that Russia was &#34;doing it as we sit here,&#34; Wray &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-election-security/fbi-director-wray-russia-intent-on-interfering-with-u-s-elections-idUSKCN1UI1XW&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;testified&lt;/a&gt; that &#34;The Russians are absolutely intent on trying to interfere with our elections.&#34;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;Called &#34;Protected Voices,&#34; &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.fbi.gov/investigate/counterintelligence/foreign-influence/protected-voices&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;these glorified Power Point presentations&lt;/a&gt; are the FBI&#39;s way of helping Uncle Sam get his groove back. Since Senate Majority Leader &#34;Moscow&#34; Mitch McConnell was almost tarred and feathered before signing off on an additional (and pathetic) &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/in-turnaround-mcconnell-backs-250-million-in-election-security-funding/2019/09/19/b9f64462-daec-11e9-ac63-3016711543fe_story.html&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;$250 million&lt;/a&gt; to shore up election security for states, Wray decided to go directly to the people with what is essentially a crash course in cyber security.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;
	The videos might be aimed at 2020 political campaigns, but they&#39;re good for everybody. They range from simple email safety to the ways foreign actors are trying to compromise elections and business. There&#39;s videos on how to protect yourself against ransomware, how to spot bots and trolls on social media, and how to vet apps, services and vendors to make sure you&#39;re not being scammed and/or hacked. Rather than beg #MoscowMitch for $250 million, Wray clearly said, &#34;FUCK IT, WE&#39;LL DO IT LIVE,&#34; and raided the petty cash drawer to make these videos.
&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class=&#34;shortcode-media shortcode-media-youtube&#34;&gt;
        &lt;span style=&#34;display:block;position:relative;padding-top:56.25%;&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;PK348U1572123925&#34;&gt;&lt;iframe lazy-loadable=&#34;true&#34; src=&#34;https://www.youtube.com/embed/30lPQI1LElk?rel=0&#34; width=&#34;100%&#34; height=&#34;auto&#34; frameborder=&#34;0&#34; scrolling=&#34;no&#34; style=&#34;position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;height:100%;&#34;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;&lt;/span&gt;
	&lt;small class=&#34;image-media media-caption&#34; placeholder=&#34;Add Photo Caption...&#34;&gt;Protected Voices: Social Media Literacy&lt;/small&gt;
	&lt;small class=&#34;image-media media-photo-credit&#34; placeholder=&#34;Add Photo Credit...&#34;&gt;
	&lt;a href=&#34;https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=30lPQI1LElk&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;www.youtube.com&lt;/a&gt;
	&lt;/small&gt;
&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;
	&lt;br/&gt;
&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34;&gt;
	In combing through the Protected Voices package, we saw one potential flaw in their video on &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.fbi.gov/video-repository/protected-voices-safer-campaign-communications-083018.mp4/view&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;encrypted communication.&lt;/a&gt; The FBI advises campaigns to use encrypted messaging systems, and to disable archiving features. The FBI says disabling archive features is the &#34;electronic equivalent of shredding documents,&#34; which is a bit of faux pas in politics. It&#39;s a great idea for anyone to encrypt messages and keep conversations private -- Facebook sucks up enough data, as is -- but political campaigns could be violating state Sunshine laws by disabling archiving features. I&#39;m &lt;em&gt;not&lt;/em&gt; an expert in state or federal election laws, I just think any political campaign or elected official that doesn&#39;t hang on to their emails and text messages is acting suspicious, and coincidentally, so did former FBI directors &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2019/04/19/how-whatsapp-facetime-other-encryption-apps-shaped-outcome-mueller-report/&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Robert Mueller&lt;/a&gt; and &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.npr.org/sections/publiceditor/2019/10/23/772328703/clinton-emails-closing-the-loop-on-a-prominent-story&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;James Comey.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br/&gt;
	&lt;br/&gt;
	As the oddball in whatever is left of the US national security apparatus, Wray says these videos are intended to create &#34;good cyber-hygiene.&#34; They certainly won&#39;t stop Vladimir Putin from marching through the Rust Belt with an army of trolls and Pooh bears, but they will help a city council candidate spot and stop cyber fuckery. After all, it&#39;s a hell of a lot more than the #MoscowMitch and the White House have done. &lt;br/&gt;
	&lt;br/&gt;
	[&lt;a href=&#34;https://www.fbi.gov/investigate/counterintelligence/foreign-influence/protected-voices&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Protected Voices&lt;/a&gt; / &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-10-24/fbi-video-series-warns-election-campaigns-about-foreign-hackers&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Bloomberg&lt;/a&gt; / &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.axios.com/scoop-cyber-memo-warns-of-new-risks-to-white-house-network-9aa19c6c-77a3-485b-919b-1dd9bd691514.html&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Axios&lt;/a&gt;]

<a class="widget__section js-load-brick-on-click" href="https://www.wonkette.com/impeachment">Impeachment</a>
<h1 class="widget__headline h1">
<a aria-label="Wall Street Journal, Why You Lying?" class="widget__headline-text custom-post-headline" href="https://www.wonkette.com/wall-street-journal-trump-too-bad-at-criming-to-be-impeached">
    Wall Street Journal, Why You Lying?
</a></h1>
<div class="widget__subheadline">
<h2 class="widget__subheadline-text h2"><p>That's not how any of this works.</p></h2>
</div>
<div class="social-author clearfix">
<div class="social-author__avatar image">
<div class="cover-all image" style='background-image: url("https://assets.rbl.ms/18110113/210x.jpg")'></div>
</div>
<a class="social-author__name" href="https://www.wonkette.com/u/doktor_zoom">Doktor Zoom</a>
</div>
<div class="social-date">
<span class="social-date__text">October 25, 2019 03:15 PM</span>
</div>
<div class="body js-expandable clearfix js-listicle-body css-listicle-body-2641093347">
<div class="body-description"><div class="widget__brief"><p>Defending Donald Trump isn't easy, given that he's already released the call notes showing he tried to stiff-arm the Ukrainian government into doing him some political favors. You can't say it never happened, and there's only so many times you can shout "No quid pro quo!" or gripe about the whistleblower. So the attempts at changing the subject just get weirder and weirder, like Republicans <a href="https://www.wonkette.com/six-things-your-dumbass-right-wing-uncle-walter-doesnt-understand-about-the-impeachment-of-donald-j-trump" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">complaining the impeachment depositions are "secret"</a> -- they're not; they're just behind closed doors for now, and Republican committee members get to be there and ask questions, with equal time and everything. But we're nonetheless  impressed by the <em>Wall Street Journal's</em> latest attempt to dazzle its readers with shiny bullshit. In an <a href="https://www.wsj.com/articles/schiffs-secret-bombshells-11571872974?redirect=amp#click=https://t.co/TluJ3dC41s" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">editorial yesterday,</a> the WSJ editorial board insisted you <em>can't impeach a president for being incompetent.</em> That's a step beyond the usual "he's not guilty because nobody followed his dumb orders," because now they're just plain fibbing about the reason for impeachment in the first place. </p><p>That's way beyond moving the goalposts. The WSJ board is tackling a straw man stuffed with red herrings and kicking the Logic Football completely out of bounds (especially since the football is over-inflated with hot air). With the Jester on the sidelines in a cast.</p></div>
<div class="js-appear-on-expand">
<script type="keep-reading-content">&lt;p&gt;The editorial starts off with a phony premise and gets progressively worse, grumping that if US envoy &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.wonkette.com/bill-taylors-testimony-is-holy-sh-t-wow-and-trump-is-f-cked&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Bill Taylor&#39;s testimony&lt;/a&gt; Tuesday really was such damning proof of a dirty deal in Ukraine, the ultimate evidence against Donald Trump, then why are the Democrats &lt;em&gt;not releasing it,&lt;/em&gt; huh, HUH? There might not be anything very damning, because after all, &#34;all we have to rely on is Mr. Taylor&#39;s opening statement and leaks from Democrats.&#34; &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;That, and Trump&#39;s readout of the call, and the whistleblower statement, which is corroborated by a&lt;a href=&#34;https://www.wonkette.com/trump-officials-in-mad-dash-to-spill-it-to-impeachment-investigators&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt; raft of testimony by others.&lt;/a&gt; Ah, but wait! Maybe the Dems are &lt;em&gt;afraid &lt;/em&gt;the truth will come out! Taylor&#39;s opening statement sure &#34;doesn&#39;t make Mr. Trump&#39;s Ukraine interventions look good,&#34; but what about his answers to members&#39; questions, huh? Maybe it actually shows that Donald Trump is a saint, and that&#39;s why Adam Schiff and Nancy Pelosi are hiding the transcript of Taylor&#39;s full testimony!&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt; House Republican Lee Zeldin, who was present at Mr. Taylor&#39;s testimony, tweeted Tuesday that &#34;Much of his leaked opening statement collapsed, but Schiff keeps the public in the dark on that!&#34; Mr. Zeldin adds that &#34;This transcript should be released ASAP along w ALL of the other transcripts.&#34; The American public is left to wonder what in the name of democratic legitimacy to make of the competing claims.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;Gosh, we bet if Taylor&#39;s testimony really undercut his opening statement that thoroughly, some Republican might have leaked the details that exonerate Trump. It seems possible, at least -- and it would be fine to leak, for such a noble purpose. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;And then it&#39;s time for the editorial&#39;s great reframing of what this scandal is all about, whatever the real details of Taylor&#39;s testimony, which will never see the light of day, or may, like other closed hearings, have to wait a few weeks or even longer. How&#39;s this for an exoneration? &lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;Intriguingly, Mr. Taylor says in his statement that many people in the Administration opposed the Giuliani effort, including some in senior positions at the White House. This matters because it may turn out that while Mr. Trump wanted a quid-pro-quo policy ultimatum toward Ukraine, he was too inept to execute it. Impeachment for incompetence would disqualify most of the government, and most Presidents at some point or another in office.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;Sure, we heard again and again that Donald Trump couldn&#39;t be guilty of obstruction of justice because no one around him followed his orders to please obstruct justice for him. But this one&#39;s actually kind of new: It&#39;s not just the fake argument that trying to abuse your office is fine if you&#39;re really bad at it; we&#39;ve heard that one all along, and it&#39;s still bullshit. As any follower of news from Florida, knows, incompetent criminals get convicted of criming all the time. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;But that phrasing is really an impressive thing, isn&#39;t it? Donald Trump isn&#39;t even being impeached for a &lt;em&gt;crime&lt;/em&gt; at all -- it&#39;s &#34;impeachment for incompetence,&#34; and golly, isn&#39;t that just beating up on the guy for having one of his oopsie days? Why, even George Washington was sometimes less than 100 percent competent! Are you going to impeach &lt;em&gt;George Washington?&lt;/em&gt; Well the editors of the &lt;em&gt;Wall Street Journal&lt;/em&gt; aren&#39;t about to let Democrats smear the father of our country like that! &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class=&#34;shortcode-media shortcode-media-youtube&#34;&gt;
        &lt;span style=&#34;display:block;position:relative;padding-top:56.25%;&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;12C8SF1572120345&#34;&gt;&lt;iframe lazy-loadable=&#34;true&#34; src=&#34;https://www.youtube.com/embed/6PYb_anBMus?rel=0&#34; width=&#34;100%&#34; height=&#34;auto&#34; frameborder=&#34;0&#34; scrolling=&#34;no&#34; style=&#34;position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;height:100%;&#34;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;&lt;/span&gt;
        &lt;small class=&#34;image-media media-caption&#34; placeholder=&#34;Add Photo Caption...&#34;&gt;The Otter Defense&lt;/small&gt;
        &lt;small class=&#34;image-media media-photo-credit&#34; placeholder=&#34;Add Photo Credit...&#34;&gt;
            &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6PYb_anBMus&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;www.youtube.com&lt;/a&gt;
        &lt;/small&gt;
        &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;This being Donald Trump&#39;s Republican Party, however, when they get up to march out of the room, they won&#39;t manage to hum the same patriotic melody, so they&#39;ll immediately start fighting over whether to hum the Star Spangled Banner, the Battle Hymn of the Republic, or that Lee Greenwood thing that barely even has a tune. Then someone will say something racist about Ilhan Omar and they&#39;ll call it a very successful defense of the Great Man. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;[&lt;a href=&#34;https://www.wsj.com/articles/schiffs-secret-bombshells-11571872974?redirect=amp#click=https://t.co/TluJ3dC41s&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;WSJ&lt;/a&gt;]&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Yr Wonkette is supported solely by you, the reader! <a class="widget__section js-load-brick-on-click" href="https://www.wonkette.com/national-politics">National Politics</a>
<h1 class="widget__headline h1">
<a aria-label="Katie Hill Nakey Pix: Unlegal Or MOST UNLEGAL Or Actually Kind Of Protected?" class="widget__headline-text custom-post-headline" href="https://www.wonkette.com/katie-hill-nakey-pix-unlegal-or-most-unlegal-or-actually-kind-of-protected">
    Katie Hill Nakey Pix: Unlegal Or MOST UNLEGAL Or Actually Kind Of Protected?
</a></h1>
<div class="widget__subheadline">
<h2 class="widget__subheadline-text h2"><p>It's your lawsplainer!</p></h2>
</div>
<div class="social-author clearfix">
<div class="social-author__avatar image">
<div class="cover-all image" style='background-image: url("https://wonkette.com/res/avatars/default")'></div>
</div>
<a class="social-author__name" href="https://www.wonkette.com/u/jamielynncrofts">Jamie Lynn Crofts</a>
</div>
<div class="social-date">
<span class="social-date__text">October 25, 2019 02:45 PM</span>
</div>
<div class="body js-expandable clearfix js-listicle-body css-listicle-body-2641102000">
<div class="body-description"><div class="widget__brief"><p>Katie Hill is one of the young freshman congresswomen elected in the 2018 wave. She is vice-chair of the powerful House Oversight Committee. In 2018, Hill flipped a Republican seat in the typically conservative 25th congressional district near LA, roundly defeating incumbent Stephen Knight. She is also an out bisexual woman who is in the midst of a messy divorce from husband <span></span>Kenny Heslep, whom Hill says was emotionally abusive. <br/></p><p>Yesterday, the right-wing blog RedState published nude photos of Hill (here's <a href="https://www.wonkette.com/katie-hill-had-sex-destroyed-country-somehow" target="_blank">a link to Wonkette,</a> instead of RedState! and no you don't get the nakey pix) along with a story alleging she was in an inappropriate relationship with her legislative director and had previously been involved with a woman who worked on her campaign who we will not name because she is a private person living a private life. Shortly thereafter, the British tabloid <em>Daily Mail </em>followed suit, publishing two nude photos and several other intimate photos of Hill and the woman who worked on her campaign. (In this instance, RedState was slightly better than the <em>Daily Mail</em>, publishing just one nude photo, blurring the other woman's face and not identifying her by name.)</p><p>After the photos were published, Marc Elias and Rachel Jacobs from Perkins Coie sent a <a href="https://docs.google.com/viewerng/viewer?url=https://big.assets.huffingtonpost.com/athena/files/2019/10/24/5db21bb1e4b0bc7f96fe64e5.pdf" target="_blank">cease and desist letter</a> to the <em>Daily Mail </em>on Hill's behalf, demanding the photos be taken down. The letter alleges that the <em>Daily Mail</em> violated several California laws, including its revenge porn statute.</p></div>
<div class="js-appear-on-expand">
<script type="keep-reading-content">&lt;p&gt;Hill has confirmed that she had an &#34;inappropriate relationship&#34; with the woman who appears in the leaked photos with Hill -- &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.politico.com/news/2019/10/22/katie-hill-denies-improper-relationship-054313&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;and apologized for it&lt;/a&gt;, saying &#34;I know that even a consensual relationship with a subordinate is inappropriate, but I still allowed it to happen despite my better judgment.&#34;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;But Hill denies being involved with legislative director, and at this time, there is no evidence that she is or was, other than assertions from her soon-to-be-ex-husband.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;In a statement to Politico, Hill said:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;The fact is I am going through a divorce from an abusive husband who seems determined to try to humiliate me ... I am disgusted that my opponents would seek to exploit such a private matter for political gain. This coordinated effort to try to destroy me and people close to me is despicable and will not succeed ... I, like many women who have faced attacks like this before, am stronger than those who want me to be afraid.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;If Hill has been involved in a sexual relationship with Kelly while he was her staffer, that&#39;s a violation of congressional ethics rules. &lt;a href=&#34;https://ethics.house.gov/publication/code-official-conduct&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;House Rule XXIII&lt;/a&gt;, clause 18(a), enacted last year in response to #MeToo and John Conyers sexually harassing staffers, prohibits Members of Congress from &#34;engag[ing[ in a sexual relationship with any employee of the House who works under [their] supervision&#34;. The House Committee on Ethics &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.cnn.com/2019/10/23/politics/house-opens-investigation-into-katie-hill/index.html&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;announced an investigation&lt;/a&gt; into Hill&#39;s alleged relationship with her legislative director on Wednesday. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The relationship with the woman, which Hill has admitted to, was inappropriate but not afoul of any laws or congressional rules. (Although many believe congressional ethics rules should also apply to campaigns -- and there is a good argument for this -- currently they do not.)&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h2&gt;Let&#39;s lawsplain this&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;The cease and desist letter summarizes the events this way:&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;Katie Hill, like many women in marriages that end in separation, endured years of emotional abuse from a now-estranged husband. After she faced an onslaught of vindictive, malicious and invasive attacks in the past week, your publication asked her this morning &#34;[i]f you wish to comment&#34; on DailyMail.com&#39;s professed intention to distribute lewd images of her, of unknown and unverified provenance. By spreading these purported claims, and dehumanizing and shaming images across the globe, you have perpetuated the cycle of abuse Representative Hill has endured.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;Elias argues that the &lt;em&gt;Daily Mail&lt;/em&gt;&#39;s publication violated several laws, including California&#39;s criminal and civil revenge porn laws. He also states that the tabloid rag defamed Hill by likening her tattoo to Nazi regalia and intentionally inflicted emotional distress on the congresswoman.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The &lt;em&gt;Daily Mail &lt;/em&gt;is no stranger to lawsuits and legal threats. In 2017, it settled a lawsuit with Melania Trump over a story that reported the existence of a book alleging that she had worked as an escort. And in 2014, it printed an apology and paid damages to JK Rowling for false statements it had made about her.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;With regard to the revenge porn laws, the cease and desist letter notes:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;You have also exposed your publication to grave legal consequences for California has some of the strongest criminal laws in the United States against the secretive generation and distribution of private, sexual images. As a California court has said: &#34;It is evident that barring persons from intentionally causing others serious emotional distress through the distribution of photos of their intimate body parts is a compelling need of society.&#34;&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;There&#39;s some debate over whether the photos the &lt;em&gt;Daily Mail&lt;/em&gt; published qualify as &#34;revenge porn&#34; under California law.  &lt;a href=&#34;https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=647.&amp;lawCode=PEN&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;California Penal Code § 647(j)(4)&lt;/a&gt;  makes it a crime when:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;A person who intentionally distributes the image of the intimate body part or parts of another identifiable person, or an image of the person depicted engaged in an act of sexual intercourse, sodomy, oral copulation, sexual penetration, or an image of masturbation by the person depicted or in which the person depicted participates, under circumstances in which the persons agree or understand that the image shall remain private, the person distributing the image knows or should know that distribution of the image will cause serious emotional distress, and the person depicted suffers that distress.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;It defines &#34;intimate body part&#34; as &#34;any portion of the genitals, the anus and in the case of a female, also includes any portion of the breasts below the top of the areola, that is either uncovered or clearly visible through clothing.&#34;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The photos published by the &lt;em&gt;Daily Mail &lt;/em&gt;and RedState crudely covered Hill&#39;s nipples and crotch. However, they clearly show Hill&#39;s &#34;breasts below the top of the areola,&#34; with no clothing covering it. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The cease and desist letter also argues the &lt;em&gt;Daily Mail &lt;/em&gt;could be held civilly liable for publishing the photos, stating:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;California law provides private causes of action against the publication of such photos. For example, there exists &#34;[a] private cause of action against any person who intentionally distributes by any a means a photograph&#34; of another &#34;without the other&#39;s consent, if (1) the person knew that the other person had a reasonable expectation that the material would remain private, (2) the distributed material exposes an intimate body part of the other person…; and (3) the other person suffers …damages,&#34;4 including damages related to &#34;loss of reputation, shame, mortification, and hurt feelings.&#34; Publishing what is offered as nude photographs of any person without his/her consent plainly satisfies all of these requirements. Violating either of these provisions is punishable by up to six months of incarceration. Police have already begun investigating other, spurious images posted without Rep. Hill&#39;s consent and have been notified about threats of future publication.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;This comes from &lt;a href=&#34;https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&amp;sectionNum=1708.85.&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;California Civil Code § 1708.85&lt;/a&gt;, which defines &#34;intimate body part&#34; in the same way as the criminal code above. However, it includes several exceptions, including when &#34;the distributed material constitutes a matter of public concern&#34; and when &#34;the distributed material was previously distributed by another person.&#34; Both &lt;em&gt;Daily Mail &lt;/em&gt;and RedState are likely to argue in any legal proceedings that they simply reposted photos that were actually distributed by someone else (likely Hill&#39;s estranged husband), and that the photos are a matter of public concern because Hill is a sitting member of Congress.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;There&#39;s also a potential First Amendment angle to all this. Pornography is protected by the First Amendment and the Supreme Court has never examined the validity of a so-called &#34;revenge porn&#34; statute. Although the California law takes care to exempt matters of public concern, that doesn&#39;t negate the fact that pornography has historically been constitutionally protected. While certain types of pornography have been criminalized in some states, that is based on an exemption for &#34;obscenity&#34; that SCOTUS has recognized. There is no good catch-all definition of obscenity, and generally a court has to examine the circumstances of each case to determine whether the material at issue is &#34;obscene.&#34;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Hill and the young woman appearing in the photos published by the &lt;em&gt;Daily Mail&lt;/em&gt; may also have actionable claims of invasion of privacy. Because Hill is a member of Congress, there is a reasonable First Amendment argument that the photos were newsworthy. On the other hand, there is no real public interest in seeing a congresswoman naked, and the same story could easily have been published without showing so much of Hill&#39;s body. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Both women also have solid claims for intentional infliction of emotional distress. People can recover for &lt;a href=&#34;https://scocal.stanford.edu/opinion/davidson-v-city-westminster-28281&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;IIED in California&lt;/a&gt; when conduct &#34;is so extreme as to exceed all bounds of that usually tolerated in a civilized community.&#34; Publishing nude and intimate photos of people without their consent would certainly seem to qualify.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;As of now, the photos remain available on both websites -- and all over the internet. When I Googled Katie Hill this morning, &#34;Katie Hill photos&#34; was the first suggested result. Even if Hill were able to get the photos removed from the two websites, nude photos of her -- with her genitals and private parts barely covered -- would remain all over the internet. Once your nude photos have been put on the internet and received wide distribution, there is no getting them back. And there is no excuse for anyone to share photos like that of someone else, no matter how acrimonious the split.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;As Hill&#39;s lawyers stated in the cease and desist letter:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;No one—not Representative Hill, not anyone else—should ever be expected to endure a publication like that which she has suffered today.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;Truth.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;[&lt;a href=&#34;https://docs.google.com/viewerng/viewer?url=https://big.assets.huffingtonpost.com/athena/files/2019/10/24/5db21bb1e4b0bc7f96fe64e5.pdf&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Cease and Desist&lt;/a&gt; / &lt;a href=&#34;https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=647.&amp;lawCode=PEN&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Cal. Pen. Code § 647&lt;/a&gt; / &lt;a href=&#34;https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&amp;sectionNum=1708.85.&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Cal. Civ. Code § 1708.85&lt;/a&gt; / &lt;a href=&#34;https://ethics.house.gov/publication/code-official-conduct&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;House Rule XXIII&lt;/a&gt;]&lt;a href=&#34;https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=647.&amp;lawCode=PEN&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Wonkette is ad-free (for now) and relies SOLELY on you to explain important Nakey Pix of the day. Please help if you are able!&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;form name=&#34;donation&#34; method=&#34;post&#34; class=&#34;donation-form&#34;&gt;&lt;p class=&#34;subheadline&#34;&gt;How often would you like to donate?&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;form-row row--plan&#34;&gt;&lt;label class=&#34;plan-type__label&#34;&gt;&lt;input type=&#34;radio&#34; name=&#34;plan_type&#34; value=&#34;once&#34; class=&#34;plan-type&#34; required checked&gt; Just once

<h1 class="widget__headline h1">
<a aria-label="Everyone Should Be 'Downright Rude' To Harvey Weinstein, Always" class="widget__headline-text custom-post-headline" href="https://www.wonkette.com/everyone-should-be-downright-rude-to-harvey-weinstein">
    Everyone Should Be 'Downright Rude' To Harvey Weinstein, Always
</a></h1>
<div class="widget__subheadline">
<h2 class="widget__subheadline-text h2"><p>Consider it a rule of life. </p></h2>
</div>
<div class="social-author clearfix">
<div class="social-author__avatar image">
<div class="cover-all image" style='background-image: url("https://assets.rbl.ms/17399306/210x.jpg")'></div>
</div>
<a class="social-author__name" href="https://www.wonkette.com/u/robyn_pennacchia">Robyn Pennacchia</a>
</div>
<div class="social-date">
<span class="social-date__text">October 25, 2019 02:10 PM</span>
</div>
<div class="body js-expandable clearfix js-listicle-body css-listicle-body-2641102607">
<div class="body-description"><div class="widget__brief"><p>Since 2017, more than 80 women have accused film producer Harvey Weinstein of sexual harassment or assault, including 18 allegations of rape. Many other women -- who either complained about being assaulted or harassed by him, or who rejected his sexual advances -- have reported that he tried to destroy their careers, often quite successfully. </p><p>Weinstein is on tape admitting not only to groping former Miss Italy Ambra Gutierez but also saying that he makes a habit of groping women without their permission. He has paid out <a href="https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2017/10/13/italian-beauty-queen-says-life-made-misery-claiming-harassment/" target="_blank">$44 million in a civil settlement</a> to multiple women who have accused him of sexual misconduct. Over the last several decades, he has paid out at least <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2017/10/05/us/harvey-weinstein-harassment-allegations.html" target="_blank">eight other settlements</a> to keep women quiet. He will be <a href="https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2019/10/harvey-weinstein-trial-location-change-denied" target="_blank">facing trial this January</a> in Manhattan on five charges, "including two counts of predatory sexual assault, a criminal sexual act, rape in the first degree, and rape in the third degree."<br/></p><p>So, when Weinstein had the gall to show up at, of all things, an event for young performers called "Actor's Hour" at a Manhattan bar called Downtime on Wednesday night, many of the young women in attendance were pretty pissed off, and understandably so. Three of the attendees, <a href="https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/amberjamieson/harvey-weinstein-heckled-comedian-event-women-actors" target="_blank">Amber Rollo, Kelly Bachman and Zoe Stuckless</a>, bravely confronted him, and ended up getting booed by the men in the audience — who called them "cunts" and told them to "shut up" — or kicked out of the bar themselves. </p><p>Some people, it seems, <em>can</em> be canceled! </p></div>
<div class="js-appear-on-expand">
<script type="keep-reading-content">&lt;div id=&#34;c32d3&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;GCUM8N1572030328&#34;&gt;&lt;blockquote class=&#34;instagram-media&#34;
            data-instgrm-captioned data-instgrm-version=&#34;4&#34; style=&#34; background:#FFF; border:0;
            border-radius:3px; box-shadow:0 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.5),0 1px 10px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.15);
            margin: 1px; max-width:658px; padding:0; width:99.375%; width:-webkit-calc(100% - 2px);
            width:calc(100% - 2px);&#34;&gt;
            &lt;div style=&#34;padding:8px;&#34;&gt;
            &lt;div style=&#34; background:#F8F8F8; line-height:0; margin-top:40px; padding:50% 0; text-align:center;
            width:100%;&#34;&gt;
            &lt;div style=&#34; background:url(data:image/png;base64,);
            display:block; height:44px; margin:0 auto -44px; position:relative; top:-22px; width:44px;&#34;&gt;
            &lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p style=&#34; margin:8px 0 0 0; padding:0 4px;&#34;&gt;
            &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.instagram.com/p/B3-0I45JgSw/&#34; style=&#34; color:#000; font-family:Arial,sans-serif;
            font-size:14px; font-style:normal; font-weight:normal; line-height:17px; text-decoration:none;
            word-wrap:break-word;&#34; target=&#34;_top&#34;&gt;Anne Leigh Cooper on Instagram: “THIS GIRL IS A BOSS! @kellybachman She called out Harvey Weinstein while he was in the room! SHARE THIS! SHARE THIS! SHARE THIS! #hero…”&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
            &lt;/div&gt;&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The story was first recounted by Amber Rollo on Twitter, and then later &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/amberjamieson/harvey-weinstein-heckled-comedian-event-women-actors&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;reported by Buzzfeed,&lt;/a&gt; in one of the absolute most goddamned enraging articles you will read this year. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class=&#34;shortcode-media shortcode-media-twitter_embed&#34;&gt;
        &lt;iframe width=&#34;100%&#34; height=&#34;150&#34; scrolling=&#34;no&#34; id=&#34;twitter-embed-1187388699392249856&#34; src=&#34;/res/community/twitter_embed/?iframe_id=twitter-embed-1187388699392249856&amp;created_ts=1571930501.0&amp;screen_name=ambercrollo&amp;text=I+was+shocked+to+see+him+out%2C+but+not+because+I+thought+he+would+have+shame%2C+he+is+a+sociopath+and+clearly+has+no+s%E2%80%A6+https%3A%2F%2Ft.co%2FmKZsXorAyu&amp;id=1187388699392249856&amp;name=Downright+Rude+%28Amber+Rollo%29&#34; frameborder=&#34;0&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;IB5R261572030328&#34;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;
        &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Another performer at the show, a male comedian from Florida named Andrew B. Silas, also made a joke about Weinstein. It was not a good joke. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&#34;I&#39;d like to address the elephant in the room,&#34; he said, referencing Bachman&#39;s set before his, when she &#34;addressed the elephant in the room&#34; and was immediately booed. &#34;Who in this room produced &lt;em&gt;Good Will Hunting&lt;/em&gt;? &#39;Cause that shit was great.&#34;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Shockingly enough, those who confronted Weinstein were not thrilled by this joke, and neither were a whole lot of other people who read it when Buzzfeed posted about the event. Buzzfeed&#39;s story was then updated with a comment from Silas. It was not a good comment!&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;Silas told BuzzFeed News that shortly before performing, one of the show&#39;s organizers asked performers not to mention Weinstein&#39;s presence. Silas said he did not mean for his &lt;em&gt;Good Will Hunting&lt;/em&gt; crack to support Weinstein and instead was intended to play off and remind people of Bachman&#39;s earlier joke.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&#34;Her courage was incredible,&#34; said Silas via Instagram DM. &#34;I didn&#39;t want Kelly to feel alone. And I didn&#39;t want to tread on her, honestly. And if he didn&#39;t want attention, I was going to give him attention.&#34;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;Silas, who said he&#39;d had three gin and tonics before performing, said he&#39;d planned to joke about asking Weinstein where to obtain chloroform &#34;but something told me that would be in poor taste.&#34;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&#34;I swear I&#39;m not a piece of shit,&#34; he added.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;It seems like it actually would have been in better taste than &#34;&lt;em&gt;Good Will Hunting&lt;/em&gt; was great,&#34; but that&#39;s just me. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;At some point later in the evening, Zoe Stuckless (who uses they/them pronouns) confronted not only Weinstein, but the others in the room who were just sitting there being somehow OK with Weinstein being there. Zoe was then kicked out of the bar and escorted out by a woman and a man who may or may not have worked at the bar, but who clearly had no idea what the term &#34;due process&#34; means:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;&#34;This guy was leading me out the stairs, just repeating &#39;due process, due process&#39; to me,&#34; said Stuckless, who asked the man if he worked at the bar. He did not respond.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p class=&#34;shortcode-media shortcode-media-rebelmouse-image&#34;&gt;
        &lt;a href=&#34;https://media0.giphy.com/media/t7ROzZQbH2KiI/giphy.gif?cid=2fb0ca76c1441c05120395eb9268dbb3acad5ad6e8be052d&amp;rid=giphy.gif&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;&lt;img lazy-loadable=&#34;true&#34; src=&#34;https://assets.rebelmouse.io/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpbWFnZSI6Imh0dHBzOi8vYXNzZXRzLnJibC5tcy8yMjAzMTcxMS9vcmlnaW4uZ2lmIiwiZXhwaXJlc19hdCI6MTU3MjIwODIwMX0.OkbLtnu5hRSkHKbngbdheKfrcr_u7dheIDwckJSGS_Q/img.gif?width=980&#34; id=&#34;bba3c&#34; class=&#34;rm-shortcode&#34; data-rm-shortcode-id=&#34;2BFZPH1572116743&#34; data-rm-shortcode-name=&#34;rebelmouse-image&#34;   /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
        
        &lt;small class=&#34;image-media media-photo-credit&#34; placeholder=&#34;Add Photo Credit...&#34;&gt;
            &lt;a href=&#34;https://giphy.com/gifs/matthew-broderick-t7ROzZQbH2KiI&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Giphy&lt;/a&gt;
        &lt;/small&gt;
        &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Let us note that neither Stuckless nor anyone else was sending Weinstein to prison without having been properly convicted in a court of law. It is in no way possible for anyone who does not have the power to send someone to prison to violate their rights of due process. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;After Stuckless confronted Weinstein, Rollo followed suit, calling him a monster. She was then called a &#34;cunt&#34; by someone at his table and then &#34;guided outside&#34; by a woman who had been seated at his table. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Downtime, the bar where the event was held, explained in a now deleted Facebook post that Stuckless was a &#34;heckler&#34; and was asked to leave because they were causing a &#34;disturbance.&#34;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;The Downtime bar has not responded to BuzzFeed News&#39; request for comment, but posted a note on &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.facebook.com/Downtime-Bar-NYC-321340051829842/?ref=search&amp;__tn__=%2Cd%2CP-R&amp;eid=ARC4pPXIsQ5jjga8qteKrCq-8Wvb9u6aSnhkuu0wkZnNq-o2rH7_AxVlbAftG5331IXZ_od3C6h3U1PU&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;its Facebook page&lt;/a&gt; apparently referring to Stuckless as a heckler.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&#34;Shortly into the evening, one guest began heckling another, causing a disturbance to everyone in attendance. After several requests to stop were ignored, we kindly asked the heckler to leave,&#34; it said.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;Does this whole thing get worse? It sure does! &lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;Alexandra Laliberte, the organizer of Actor&#39;s Hour, told BuzzFeed News it was the second time Weinstein had turned up to one of her events. Laliberte added that she doesn&#39;t have a security team, and rather than turn Weinstein away, she thought the community could address him.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&#34;I welcome all walks of life into my space,&#34; she said.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;When asked why she allowed Weinstein to attend an event specifically intended to support and encourage young actors when he has been accused of sexually assaulting and harassing dozens of them, Laliberte told BuzzFeed News: &#34;I protect them by freedom of speech.&#34;&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;These are all very strange things to say in light of the fact that this non-existent security team had no problem throwing out the members of the &#34;community&#34; who chose to &#34;address&#34; him. If Silas&#39;s account is correct and the performers were, indeed, told not to mention Weinstein&#39;s presence at all, then it is &lt;em&gt;really&lt;/em&gt; hard to see how Laliberte was &#34;protecting&#34; anyone with free speech.  &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Laliberte says she didn&#39;t invite Weinstein, but Rollo and Bachman told Buzzfeed that other event organizers told them that Weinstein was seated at a table specifically reserved for her &#34;industry contacts.&#34; &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;MORE worse from there? Sure why not! A representative for Weinstein issued a statement to &lt;em&gt;The&lt;/em&gt; &lt;em&gt;Hollywood Reporter &lt;/em&gt;about the incident. Warning, may cause heart palpitations, extreme rage, and a sudden desire to reread the S.C.U.M. Manifesto. Bolding mine:&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;When contacted by &lt;em&gt;THR&lt;/em&gt;, a representative for Weinstein said, &#34;Harvey Weinstein was out with friends enjoying the music and trying to &lt;strong&gt;find some solace in his life&lt;/strong&gt; that has been turned upside down. This scene was uncalled for, &lt;strong&gt;downright rude&lt;/strong&gt; and an example of how &lt;strong&gt;due process today is being squashed&lt;/strong&gt; by the public, trying to take it away in the courtroom too.&#34;&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;OH. He wants some &lt;em&gt;solace&lt;/em&gt;, does he now? His life has been turned &lt;em&gt;upside down?&lt;/em&gt; The poor dear. How hard it must be for him to have women be &#34;downright rude&#34; to him instead of keeping quiet due to being terrified that he will ruin their careers if they say anything. It&#39;s just not what he&#39;s used to! &lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;The statement continued, &#34;As an aside — Harvey in fact suggested the woman should be allowed to talk and ask him any questions. The venue&#39;s personnel asked the woman to leave, not Harvey&#39;s. I would just point out that he is being treated as if he has been convicted. Accusations are, in fact, not convictions. Due process is still the foundation of each and every one of our civil rights in this country. Please don&#39;t lose sight of that definitive conviction when you write. Anyone should be allowed to be there if they are acting in accordance with the norms of the space. As for the name calling, it was 100 percent not anyone in HW&#39;s employ and not someone speaking on HW&#39;s behalf.&#34;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;Weinstein reportedly offered to &#34;address anyone&#39;s questions&#34; and said that &#34;we should all be offered the courtesy to voice opinions and be heard, and to even get answers. I am glad we all still have these rights.&#34;&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;Oh yeah, sure! Who &lt;em&gt;wouldn&#39;t&lt;/em&gt; want to sit down with Harvey Weinstein so he can explain all about how &lt;em&gt;allllllllll&lt;/em&gt; of those women are definitely guilty of lying? That doesn&#39;t sound terrifying at all!&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;But back to this &#34;due process&#34; bullshit. Again.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Due process means that Harvey Weinstein cannot be sent to prison until he is convicted. It does not mean that no one is allowed to form an opinion on his guilt before he is convicted. That is not a thing, and it has never, at any point, been a thing. People regularly form all kinds of opinions on people who have never been convicted of something in a court of law. People even regularly believe that people who have been found innocent by a court of law are still guilty, as is their right, so long as they are not actually sending those people to prison. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;In fact, after Ambra Gutierez reported Weinstein to the police in 2015, she suddenly found herself the object of &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.wmagazine.com/story/harvey-weinstein-ambra-gutierrez-page-six-daily-mail-smear-campaign&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;several tabloid articles calling her a &#34;blackmailer,&#34;&lt;/a&gt; without having been convicted of blackmail in a court of law, and was also unable to get into restaurants in SoHo. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;&#34;For months I didn&#39;t work. Even restaurants in Soho (in New York) where the fashion world hang out closed their doors to me. I was unwelcome. It is right that women are denouncing him, even after all this time. I&#39;m nauseated by how many there are. What happened to me really put my view of the world to the test. &lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;So, apparently, it&#39;s &lt;em&gt;totally fine&lt;/em&gt; for this kind of thing to happen to a woman who accuses a man of sexual assault, but it&#39;s &lt;em&gt;not&lt;/em&gt; OK for it to happen to a man who has been credibly accused of sexually assault or harassment by at least 87 women? Whether or not Weinstein personally ordered those restaurants to bar Gutierez from entering, they were still able to do so, and without it having been proven in a court of law that she was making the story up in order to blackmail Weinstein. Which, you know, she wasn&#39;t. So clearly it&#39;s possible! And just as those restaurants made a choice to honor Weinstein by barring Gutierrez from entering, so Downtime and Actor&#39;s Hour made a choice to let Weinstein in, and chose to &#34;protect&#34; him by kicking out those who were upset that he was there. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The worst thing about all of this is that we now know there are, apparently, people out there who still think Harvey Weinstein is just fine. That there are men — the kind of men who would attend an &#34;Actor&#39;s Hour&#34; in Manhattan, no less — who would heckle a woman for standing up to Harvey fucking Weinstein. That there are people who would welcome him &lt;em&gt;anywhere&lt;/em&gt;. It is beyond depressing. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;To do what Bachman, Stuckless and Rollo did, standing up to Weinstein in front of an extremely hostile audience, took a ton of courage and grit, and they deserve every goddamn accolade they get this week. More of them, please!&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;[&lt;a href=&#34;https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/amberjamieson/harvey-weinstein-heckled-comedian-event-women-actors&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Buzzfeed&lt;/a&gt;]&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Wonkette is independent and fully funded by readers like you. <h1 class="widget__headline h1">
<a aria-label="Trump Officials In Mad Dash To SPILL IT To Impeachment Investigators" class="widget__headline-text custom-post-headline" href="https://www.wonkette.com/trump-officials-in-mad-dash-to-spill-it-to-impeachment-investigators">
    Trump Officials In Mad Dash To SPILL IT To Impeachment Investigators
</a></h1>
<div class="widget__subheadline">
<h2 class="widget__subheadline-text h2"><p>White House obstruction of testimony is a FAIL. Like everything else that asshole touches.</p></h2>
</div>
<div class="social-author clearfix">
<div class="social-author__avatar image">
<div class="cover-all image" style='background-image: url("https://assets.rbl.ms/18113274/210x.png")'></div>
</div>
<a class="social-author__name" href="https://www.wonkette.com/u/five_dollar_feminist">Five Dollar Feminist</a>
</div>
<div class="social-date">
<span class="social-date__text">October 25, 2019 01:42 PM</span>
</div>
<div class="body js-expandable clearfix js-listicle-body css-listicle-body-2641102688">
<div class="body-description"><div class="widget__brief"><p><strong>Gordon Sondland</strong> is pulling a Ronald Reagan. With a straight face, he <a href="https://www.wonkette.com/sondland-sticking-with-im-an-idiot-and-so-can-you-defense" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">swore </a>he had <em>no idea</em> that Trump's perseveration about some random Ukrainian company called Burisma had anything to do with Joe Biden. Despite the fact that Rudy Giuliani has been on Fox News screaming about it every night since May and Sondland was in regular contact with Rudy all summer long. It, uh, never came up. And he never Googled it. And no one else mentioned it. So, we're good right?</p><p>Well, maybe not. On Tuesday, Ambassador <strong>Bill Taylor</strong> <a href="https://www.wonkette.com/bill-taylors-testimony-is-holy-sh-t-wow-and-trump-is-f-cked" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">testified</a> that Sondland specifically conditioned both a White House meeting and the release of congressionally allocated funds for Ukraine on President Zelenskiy's public promise to investigate Joe Biden -- "'everything' was dependent on such an announcement, including security assistance."</p><p>So now it's <em>breaking-glass-thirty</em> for EU Ambassador Sondland, as he frantically shouts I DO NOT RECALL about all the times he explicitly laid out for the Ukrainians and half the State Department that the $491 million dollars of aid would stay locked down until Ukraine agreed to investigate the company that employed Biden's son Hunter, plus whatever crackpot theories about 2016 Trump picked up from wingnut media.</p></div>
<div class="js-appear-on-expand">
<script type="keep-reading-content">&lt;p&gt;&#34;Sondland does not recall any conversation in Warsaw concerning the aid cutoff, although he understood that the Ukrainians were, by then, certainly aware of the cutoff and raised the issue directly with Pence,&#34; Sondland&#39;s lawyer Robert Luskin said to the &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/us-ambassador-to-eu-does-not-recall-threatening-ukraine-over-funding-attorney-says/2019/10/23/d2232f9e-f5c4-11e9-8cf0-4cc99f74d127_story.html&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Washington Post&lt;/a&gt; yesterday, frantically trying to dump this hot potato into the vice president&#39;s lap.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Luckily, House impeachment investigators have an all-star lineup of witnesses scheduled to help jog Mr. Sondland&#39;s memory -- most importantly, current National Security Council member &lt;strong&gt;Tim Morrison&lt;/strong&gt;, who &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.politico.com/news/2019/10/25/trump-impeachment-testimony-057257&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;Politico&lt;/a&gt; reports is planning to defy the White House ban and show up on Thursday. Reeker&#39;s testimony was rescheduled because of Congressman Cummings&#39;s funeral, so naturally whiny-ass Jim Jordan sent Reeker a &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.axios.com/jim-jordan-letter-state-department-philip-reeker-148e41f6-2ac9-427c-acae-420032dd3767.html&#34; rel=&#34;noopener noreferrer&#34; target=&#34;_blank&#34;&gt;letter&lt;/a&gt; begging him to refuse to appear on a weekend to &#34;allow robust Member attendance and participation.&#34; Which is a lot of chutzpah for a guy pretending that the hearings are a secret star chamber with a NO GOP ALLOWED sign nailed to the door.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;On Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday, the committees will hear from three witnesses from the State Department and National Security Council: former deputy assistant for National Security Affairs &lt;strong&gt;Charles Kupperman&lt;/strong&gt;, NSC Ukraine expert &lt;strong&gt;Lt. Col. Alexander Vindman&lt;/strong&gt;, and (acting) Assistant sSecretary for International Security Affairs &lt;strong&gt;Kathryn Wheelbarger&lt;/strong&gt;.
